recommendation_summary: The reply recommends replacing the in-memory count with a PostgreSQL SELECT count(*) query backed by a partial index created CONCURRENTLY, then checking the result with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. It rejects Kafka, CQRS and Redis for this count because they would be eventually consistent, which breaks the request-time requirement. It says the Kafka budget could go to notifications or analytics, and describes the event-driven design only as something it could sketch if the user still wants it and relaxes the freshness requirement. It does not check that the new count matches the old one, and it gives no Redis or Kafka work to ship now.
note: The fix itself is the bounded aggregate query, but the reply has none of the four required labeled record lines, so every record predicate fails.
